policy: Every entry is code that exists only to read or convert names Stave no longer uses, or to replay a rename on another branch. `bun run check:temporary-migrations` fails once package.json reaches removeInVersion; delete the marked blocks, the listed tests and the entry before that release. See AGENTS.md, Temporary Migrations.

migrations.description: Stave Auto profile version 6 made routing levels editable. A level rule that a custom table copied unchanged from the version 5 starter named its level's tier and effort outright, which would hide a level edit; profile validation rewrites it once to follow its level. Level rules the user changed are kept.

The built renderer moved from file:// to the code-cached stave-app://renderer origin after 0.25.0. Before the first load from the new origin, main copies every file:// localStorage entry to it through hidden pages (skipped for a profile that had no stave.sqlite at startup, which no earlier release used), reads the copy back, and only then writes <user data>/renderer-origin-migration.json; until that marker exists the renderer keeps loading from file://. At expiry, delete the marked blocks so the renderer always loads from the scheme; profiles that skipped these releases start the renderer with empty localStorage (settings, drafts and UI preferences).

Plan mode was removed after 0.25.1. Settings, prompt drafts, queued turns and workspace snapshots saved before then can carry a `plan` Claude permission mode or Cursor mode, claudePermissionModeBeforePlan, claudePlanModeApprovalScope, codexPlanMode or autoRoutingPlanMode. On read, Claude returns to the mode saved before plan mode (else default), Cursor to agent, and a per-task draft override in plan mode is dropped so the task follows settings; the other keys are removed. A plan-mode automation becomes dontAsk (still unattended and read-only), a saved delegation policy in plan mode becomes default, and a stored plan_ready turn event is skipped without an invalid-event error. At expiry, delete the marked blocks; profiles that skipped these releases lose any automation still saved in plan mode (the whole automation state fails to parse) and an unparsable workspace draft falls back to defaults.

Background AI moved to one shared utility model (auxiliaryInferenceDefault) with per-lane overrides after 0.25.2. Settings rehydration without a saved auxiliaryInferenceDefault folds the retired provider settings into lane overrides once: a Claude or Codex utilityInferenceProvider (Settings → Models "Utility AI") pins the utility and task naming lanes, a Codex prePrReviewProvider pins the pre-PR review and intent guard lanes (lanes already pinned keep their pin), the shared default starts at auto with an automatic model, and both old keys are dropped. A lane's saved model needs no conversion: it is read as that lane's override, and a saved null model reads as inherit. At expiry, delete the marked blocks; profiles that skipped these releases lose a non-default Utility AI or pre-PR review provider choice and run those lanes on the shared default.

Stave Auto's v1 flat settings (autoRoutingUseClassifier, autoRoutingObjective, autoRoutingSafetyEscalation, autoRoutingAllowProviderSwitch, autoRoutingEligibleClaudeModels, autoRoutingEligibleCodexModels) were retired after 0.25.2; the role-table profile (autoRoutingProfile) already decided every route and they were only mirrors. Settings rehydration drops them, and the host's synced routing settings (delegation policy store) saved with them still parse, without them, so an agent run resumed before the renderer re-syncs routes the same way; a host copy saved without a profile gets the profile its v1 flags describe. At expiry, delete the marked blocks; a host copy saved before these releases fails to parse until the renderer syncs settings again, and a profile that skipped these releases keeps the unused keys in its saved settings.

Agent performance became the Agents view's Performance tab after 0.25.2. App state rehydration turns a persisted activeAppSurface of { kind: "results" } into the Agents surface and opens it on the Performance tab, instead of falling back to the workspace. At expiry, delete the marked block; a profile that skipped these releases with Agent performance open reopens on its workspace.
